excluded_seen: Step 4e (examples/scale-up-closure-territories, registered and run): the still world, B23467/S4568, B24678/S34678, B3568/S124678, B2/S0 and B2578/S135678 read by who leads a block on side 1,024 from starts 15001 to 15008, 15101, 15102 and 16001 to 16504. Every bound here was drawn from those records.
The sizing look (sizing.py here, exploratory): those records again through this study's measures, with the first look's still world read at finer ticks for blocks of 16. It ran nothing.

Step 4c (examples/scale-up-territories, registered and run) ran each of the 38 rules against its copy on side 256 for 512 generations from start 14001, and read them by their correlation area and their species' shares: that is how they were chosen. None has been run on a larger grid, for longer, or read by who leads a block, and no coarse rule has been learned from one.
No start from 17001 on has been generated or run.
body.not_tested: No claim about a world is tested unless two species hold ground at the end (the larger has at most 0.8 of the live cells). A: not tested where the walls thin as a power of time between 0.33 and 0.4. P, K: not tested unless the power is 0.4 or more and the pace by the walls is between 0.2 and 5.0 (so too A, where the power is 0.4 or more); K also not unless at most 0.2 of neighbouring blocks of 8 have different leaders at generation 1,024. R: not tested over fewer than 8 worlds. And no claim is tested without a number to judge.

A, the clock.drawn from: the powers of step 4e's worlds: four at 0.46 to 0.49 that the still world's rule serves within 0.7% at some pace, one at 0.27 that it does not serve within 59%, and the control at 0 that it does not serve within 119%. The least and the most of one start are 0.40 and 0.55 for the four, 0.21 and 0.31 for the fifth; this study reads four starts a world.

F, a filling world's clock.drawn from: the filling worlds step 4e ran: the still world, its near relative and the other still world thin their walls as the 0.46th to 0.49th power of time, and the control, which fills as they do, as the 0.00th. That is four worlds. A fifth that the search followed on a large grid by another measure (B03458/S035678) started late and had not come to a steady clock by generation 2,048; it has not been read this way, and it is the kind of world that could fall between.

K, run on at its walls' pace.drawn from: step 4e's run-ons at blocks of 8 with the still world's rule: 0.37 in the busy world and 0.55 in the near one as it is (their paces by their walls are 1.09 and 0.73), 0.75 in the other still world as it is and 0.57 at half its pace (0.54 by its walls); each world's own rule gives 0.36, 0.58 and 0.61.

P, the pace two ways.drawn from: the still world's rule at this study's eleven paces, at blocks of 16, in the busy, the near and the other still world: the pace by the rule is 0.95, 1.28 and 1.05 of the pace by the walls. Blocks of 8 could not be read at these paces from runs that exist.

X, the anchor.drawn from: step 4e's own anchor: the first look's rule was within 0.03% of a rule learned from fresh starts, against bounds of 0.3% and 0.5%.

what a claim stands on.drawn from: in step 4e's worlds the larger species has 0.52 to 0.55 of the live cells at the end, 0.64 at most in one start; a block of 8 fits where at most a fifth of neighbouring blocks differ at generation 1,024, as in step 4e (0.09 to 0.12 in the four worlds served, 0.22 in the sparse one, 0.26 in the control). The paces a rule is kept at run from a quarter to four times the still world's, so a pace by the walls under 0.2 or over 5 is one no rule here is near.

body.source: docs/scale-up-plan.md, step 4e and decision D11; the worlds from the registered runs of examples/scale-up-territories
body.statement: A table of who leads a block next, read off one world of territories (the still world), is tried in 38 worlds no run has zoomed out: every rule of step 4c's runs that fills its grid, and a share of those that hold territories without filling it. A world's clock says whether the rule serves it (A); a world that fills keeps the square-root clock or has set (F); where a world keeps the square-root clock the pace at which the rule serves it is the pace its walls give (P, R) and the rule for that pace, run on by itself, keeps the world (K); and the still world's rule here is the first look's (X).
